intent: Inside Hilliard's town limits, do I need the town's permission before a turf base is dug, and which watering rules apply to my yard?
distinctValue: Hilliard is an incorporated town with its own land development code, its own water and sewer utility and its own forms, none of which appear on the neighbouring Nassau Village-Ratliff, Nassauville or Baldwin pages. Its code, Sec. 62-353, says no excavation or filling can occur on a lot unless an active permit has been issued, sends permission for excavation for site clearing to the Planning and Zoning Board, and lists one exception: four loads of fill per year on homesteaded properties. The town's Site Clearing/Site Work application (updated 1/2026) asks for a site plan, a statement of proposed work, proof of ownership, a St. Johns River Water Management District permit or letter of exception, a notarized signature and a $200 fee, confirmed in the Resolution 2026-09 fee schedule, and warns that work before approval results in a code enforcement violation. The tree article treats root damage and grade changes over roots as tree removal. Town Public Works supplies water from four Floridan aquifer wells, and its January 2026 notice bans lawn watering from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., which is looser than the district's Phase III 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. ban, still in effect on 3 September 2026. The page turns that into questions a homeowner can put to the Land Use Administrator before a dig date is set.

sources.label: Town of Hilliard Comprehensive Plan 2040 (adopted)
sources.note: Linked from the town's Planning & Zoning page as 'Adopted Comprehensive Plan 2040'. The soil map legend is extracted text from the map titled Soil Types, Town of Hilliard, dated 3/31/2020.
supports: COMPREHENSIVE PLAN 2040
Most of the businesses and residents in the Town are served by the Town's water system.
Potable water is obtained from the Floridan Aquifer. The Town has four wells each of which has a pumping capacity of 350 gallons per minute (g.p.m.).

The Floridian Aquifer lies 400-500 feet below the ground surface in the Hilliard area. In comparison to other area of the state, recharge to the Floridian Aquifer in the Hilliard area is very low. The surficial aquifer lies just below the land surface and extends through the planning area.
The Town of Hilliard is the operator of the sanitary sewer system in the town limits.
The Town does not have any reuse service areas in the town limits.

unresolved: Whether a residential turf base counts as excavation or filling under Sec. 62-353, and whether it needs the Site Clearing/Site Work application, is not stated in the code or on the form. The page sends the reader to the Land Use Administrator (904-675-6172) for a written answer before a dig date is set.

Sec. 62-353's exception for four loads of fill per year on homesteaded properties follows the Planning and Zoning Board sentence; whether it also relieves the active-permit sentence is not clear from the text. The page quotes the exception and tells the reader to ask.

Sec. 62-571 exempts one- and two-family dwelling units from the landscape requirements, and all pines from the tree section, but does not say plainly whether the Sec. 62-570 removal permit applies to a hardwood on a house lot. The page asks the reader to confirm with the Land Use Administrator.
Whether a PUD home's front-yard ground cover requirement (Sec. 62-565(a)) accepts synthetic turf is not addressed; the page frames it as a question.
The lot coverage caps count buildings and accessory structures and do not mention ground covers; the page says so and sends a reader near the cap to ask.
The 2026 Planning & Zoning deadline calendar is a scanned image with no text layer, so the page gives only the board's standing meeting day and time.
The district's watering restrictions page says 'Portions of ... Nassau ... counties within the District', while the signed order says 'All of ... Nassau'; the page follows the signed order.
